facts.statement: The genus Diplocynodon was first described by Pomel in 1847.
facts.quote: authority: Pomel, 1847

facts.statement: Fossils of Diplocynodon date from the Paleocene to the Middle Miocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Paleocene - Middle Miocene,

facts.statement: Diplocynodon was an extinct eusuchian crocodilian that lived in Europe from the Paleocene to the Middle Miocene.
facts.quote: Diplocynodon is an extinct genus of eusuchian, either an alligatoroid crocodilian or a stem-group crocodilian, that lived during the Paleocene to Middle Miocene in Europe.

facts.statement: Some species of Diplocynodon may have reached lengths of 3 meters, while others were likely smaller than 1 meter.
facts.quote: Some species may have reached lengths of 3 m, while others probably did not exceed 1 m.

facts.statement: The largest known species, D. hantoniensis, measured 5.9 meters (19.5 feet) in length.
facts.quote: The largest species D.hantoniensis measured 5.9 m (19.5 ft) in length.

facts.statement: Diplocynodon species are almost exclusively found in freshwater environments.
facts.quote: They are almost exclusively found in freshwater environments.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the various species of Diplocynodon were opportunistic aquatic predators.
facts.quote: The various species are thought to have been opportunistic aquatic predators.

facts.statement: Well-preserved specimens of Diplocynodon have been found in the Messel Pit and the Geiseltal lignite deposit in Germany.
facts.quote: Well preserved specimens have been found in the Messel Pit and the Geiseltal lignite deposit in Germany.

facts.statement: Most articulated Diplocynodon specimens from the Messel Pit and Geiseltal contain gastroliths.
facts.quote: Most articulated Diplocynodon specimens from these localities contain gastroliths.

facts.statement: Diplocynodon is considered one of the most basal members of the superfamily Alligatoroidea.
facts.quote: Diplocynodon is one of the basal-most members of the superfamily Alligatoroidea.

facts.statement: Osteohistological analysis suggests D. hantoniensis had a growth pattern similar to the modern American alligator, with determinate, seasonally-controlled growth.
facts.quote: Osteohistological analysis of D. hantoniensis suggests that it had a similar pattern of growth to the modern American alligator, exhibiting a determinate, seasonally-controlled rate of growth.

facts.statement: CT scans of D. tormis have reconstructed internal snout and brain structures, providing insights into its sensory and cognitive capabilities.
facts.quote: CT scans of D. tormis reconstruct internal structures of its snout and a portion of its brain, with implications for its sensory and cognitive capabilities.

facts.statement: Skull shape analysis suggests Diplocynodon was a small generalist carnivore that shared resources with the larger Asiatosuchus.
facts.quote: Based on skull shape analysis of the crocodylians known from the Lutetian site of Geiseltal, Diplocynodon was a small generalist carnivore that partitioned its resources with the larger Asiatosuchus.

facts.statement: Isotopic analysis of enamel from Late Oligocene specimens indicates Diplocynodon primarily fed on aquatic vertebrates.
facts.quote: According to enamel δ13C values from specimens from the Late Oligocene site of Enspel, the Diplocynodon living in the palaeoenvironment fed primarily on aquatic vertebrates.

facts.statement: Diplocynodon was similar to the modern caiman, being a small animal with a bony armor of osteoderms covering its neck, back, belly, and tail.
facts.quote: Era muy similar al actual caimán en que era un animal pequeño y poseía una armadura de escudos óseos (osteodermos) que cubrían su cuello, espalda, vientre y cola.

facts.statement: Diplocynodon lived from the Early Eocene to the Middle Miocene, approximately 49 million years ago in Europe.
facts.quote: Diplocynodon es un género extinto de aligatoroideo que vivió desde el Eoceno Inferior hasta mediados del Mioceno, hace 49 millones de años en Europa.

facts.statement: The largest Diplocynodon specimen found measured 1.2 meters in length and likely fed on fish, small terrestrial animals, and insects when young.
facts.quote: El mayor ejemplar de Diplocynodon encontrado medía 1.2 metros de largo y probablemente se alimentaba de peces, pequeños animales terrestres y de insectos cuando joven.

facts.statement: Well-preserved specimens have been found in the strata of the Messel quarry in Germany.
facts.quote: Especímenes bien preservados han sido hallados en los estratos de la cantera Messel en Alemania.

facts.statement: During the Eocene, the Messel quarry was a freshwater swamp lake that was ideal for fossil preservation due to anoxic conditions at the bottom.
facts.quote: En el período Eoceno, la cantera era un lago pantanoso de agua dulce que era perfecto para preservar fósiles debido a las condiciones anóxicas en el fondo del mismo.

facts.statement: Diplocynodon is one of the most basal members of the superfamily Alligatoroidea.
facts.quote: Diplocynodon es uno de los miembros más basales de la superfamilia Alligatoroidea.

facts.statement: Diplocynodon belongs to the alligatoroid group of reptiles known as Alligatoroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Alligatoroidea

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Diplocynodon is Diplocynodon ratelii.
facts.quote: Type species: Diplocynodon ratelii

facts.statement: Diplocynodon lived between 83.6 and 0.129 million years ago, spanning from the Campanian to the Chibanian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Chibanian (83.6 to 0.129 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 130 recorded fossil occurrences of Diplocynodon in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 130

facts.statement: A taxonomic revision of the genus Diplocynodon was published by Walter and colleagues in 2026.
facts.quote: Taxonomic revision of the genus Diplocynodon is published by Walter et al. (2026).

facts.statement: Martin and colleagues reported in 2026 that fossil material of Diplocynodon was found in Oligocene strata in central Turkey, marking one of the easternmost known records of the genus.
facts.quote: Martin et al. (2026) report the discovery of fossil material of Diplocynodon sp. from the Oligocene strata in central Turkey, representing one of the easternmost records of the genus reported to date.

rejected.statement: A 2025 study suggests that Diplocynodon may not be a true alligatoroid or even a true crocodilian, but rather a derived non-crocodilian eusuchian.
rejected.quote: In their analysis several genera traditionally viewed as basal alligatoroids, among them Diplocynodon, were found to not only fall outside of Alligatoroidea but to not even be true crocodilians, instead representing derived non-crocodilian eusuchians.
